summary: This room's five targets mostly already know their own neighbourhood — four of the five had already linked outward to every hop1 neighbour in their own frontmatter, so the real work was inbound: finding which of those neighbours (or their neighbours) owed a link back. The Substrate Drifts is the clean case — a zero-inbound seed entry whose hop1 ring (BBS Blackboard, SUBSTRATE, Project Stewardship System) are literally the systems its bugs happened on, and none of the three pointed back before this walk. Zoom Out to the Structure's hop2 ring turned up the actual RunPod story it cites as a worked example (RunPod GPU Backend, assume multi-agent) plus a genuine cross-domain bridge to Christopher Alexander's pattern language. Two targets (The Practice Rediscovers Its Philosophy, Weaving Memory into the Palace) turned out to have unsung paths — a named entry sitting unlinked in their own body prose (Trickster Commit; Worktree Practice, already wikilinked but missing from frontmatter) — worth fixing before chasing further inbound. Weaving Memory into the Palace's forward vector ("I want to become a named step in the Weave Ceremony") is stale: Weave Ceremony already links back to it (memory-home) — the aspiration has already landed and the vector should say so.

typed_relations.label: the-fix-that-became-commons
typed_relations.rationale: Zoom Out to the Structure's own worked example is 'A one-file RunPod pod-naming fix → The Commons, a whole coordination layer for any shared external service.' RunPod GPU Backend is that fix's object — its reader would want the zoom-out story of how its own scar became a general structure.
typed_relations.evidence: "A one-file RunPod pod-naming fix → The Commons, a whole coordination layer for any shared external service." (Zoom Out to the Structure.md:39)

typed_relations.label: the-scar-that-zoomed-out
typed_relations.rationale: assume multi-agent's 'scar' section (the lost RunPod day, phantom nodes) is the exact incident Zoom Out cites as its example of a small fix revealing a missing structure. The two entries narrate the same event from complementary sides.
typed_relations.evidence: "A full day (2026-07-02) looked like a RunPod outage... The real cause was a second Claude on the same account." (assume multi-agent.md:43-44)

typed_relations.label: recurring-friction-is-a-pattern
typed_relations.rationale: Zoom Out to the Structure's honest signal for 'this is a doorway, not just a bug' is recurring friction: 'when the same shape of problem keeps coming back, that repetition is the absence talking.' That is exactly Alexander's definition of a pattern — a problem that recurs in a context, worth naming and reusing. Same structure, different material (Alexander: architecture; this entry: engineering practice).
typed_relations.evidence: "The honest signal is recurring friction — when the same shape of problem keeps coming back, that repetition is the absence talking, and that's when to build the structure." (Zoom Out to the Structure.md:50)

typed_relations.label: deliberate-vs-found
typed_relations.rationale: Metaphor as Coupling Medium is the deliberate act of bridging two domains through an image; The Practice Rediscovers Its Philosophy documents the same bridge happening by accident, with nobody intending it. Worth reading together as the intentional and unintentional halves of one mechanism.

typed_relations.label: memory-earns-the-scale-shift
typed_relations.rationale: Scale-Stratified Identity dissolves 'is it still the same?' into 'same at which scale?'; The Remembering Page proposes a specific mechanism for the scale where identity is proposed to change — memory as the ledger that earns a self-edit across several encounters rather than seizing it in one. Both already link to Threshold Conatus and Identity Molting independently; this closes the triangle.

typed_relations.label: where-it-bit
typed_relations.rationale: The Substrate Drifts documents three bugs from treating the live blackboard as static — BBS Blackboard is that blackboard. Its own frontmatter already uses the label 'where-it-bit' for this relationship; the return link was simply missing.
typed_relations.evidence: "Three independent bugs in the STIGMERGY v0.3 session shared one root: the code treated the palace blackboard as static and uniform when it is in fact living and heterogeneous." (The Substrate Drifts.md:32)

typed_relations.label: pending-promotion
typed_relations.rationale: The Substrate Drifts carries an explicit editorial note asking to be promoted into SUBSTRATE.md as a standing design rule once it proves out across more tools — SUBSTRATE (the deepens-ground the target already names) should be pointing at the candidate waiting to be folded in.
typed_relations.evidence: "CLAUDE → LOUDON: candidate to promote into SUBSTRATE.md as a standing design rule once it proves out across more tools than STIGMERGY." (The Substrate Drifts.md:53)

typed_relations.label: the-accumulator-bites
typed_relations.rationale: The Substrate Drifts names Project Stewardship System as one of the four registers that make the board a moving target ('it accumulates — Project Stewardship System keeps depositing requests no one has answered yet'). The accumulator entry should point at the concrete case where its own accumulation broke something.
typed_relations.evidence: "it accumulates — [[Project Stewardship System]] keeps depositing requests no one has answered yet" (The Substrate Drifts.md:42)
